idiom_name: ?$select=Rating,ReleaseDate through the OData query options pipeline
implementation_notes: With the OData stack the caller's field list is a first-class system query option: $select names the properties per entity and composes with $expand to shape the resource graph ('$select=*' requests all structural properties). The framework builds the projection and, with EF Core, pushes it into the query so only the selected columns are read. Without the OData stack use the typed LINQ projection instead - System.Text.Json has no field selection of its own.
pitfalls: Without an EF Core projection the query materializes every column and $select only trims the serialized output.
[EnableQuery] without limits (PageSize/MaxExpansionDepth) lets a caller combine $select with $expand gradients into a denial-of-service surface.
$select naming is case/schema-sensitive and differs between OData v4 casing rules and the DTO's JSON names, so property renames silently change the accepted field vocabulary.

variants.name: LINQ Select into a typed DTO
variants.idiom_name: Enumerable.Select(...) projecting the entity into a record/DTO whose property set is the view
variants.implementation_notes: Without OData the field set becomes a compile-time type: Select the entity into a record/DTO that contains exactly the view's properties, so the compiler and (with EF Core) the query provider both know which columns matter. A runtime fields parameter then maps onto a bounded catalog of such views rather than onto arbitrary paths; anything the caller names outside the catalog is a 400, not a silent trim.
pitfalls: Projecting after FindAsync materializes the whole entity; use a projected IQueryable so EF Core issues a column-limited SELECT.
View DTOs drift from the entity: adding a field to the entity does not add it to any view, so callers silently keep getting the old shape.
Records make it tempting to hand the DTO to the deserializer as well; the projection type must not become the input contract, or callers lose the fields they cannot name.
